question: Before it became a children's toy, Play-Doh was a cleaning putty. People rolled it across something in their homes to lift off sooty grime from coal fires. What was it?
topic: Inventions that started out as something else
source_excerpt: wallpaper cleaner... remove coal residue from wallpaper in coal-heated homes

extra.why_interesting: Players assume Play-Doh was always a toy. It was actually a household cleaner. The coal-soot clue lets them work out what it cleaned.
extra.verification_notes: Wikipedia confirms Play-Doh began as a wallpaper cleaner for removing coal soot/residue.

explanation: Coal heating left soot on wallpaper, and the putty pulled it off. When homes switched to cleaner heating, sales collapsed, so the maker sold it to schools as modelling clay.

question: Super Glue was discovered by accident while chemists were trying to make see-through plastic for one part of a gun. Which part?
topic: Inventions that started out as something else
source_excerpt: Coover was at Eastman Kodak working on clear optical plastic for gun sights; the cyanoacrylate he produced was rejected because it stuck to everything.

extra.why_interesting: Players expect glue to come from a search for a better adhesive. In fact it was a failed attempt at an optical part. The clues 'see-through plastic' and 'gun' let players reason their way to the sight.
extra.verification_notes: Multiple sources agree Coover in 1942 was developing clear plastic for precision gun sights when he found cyanoacrylate; no newer developments contradict this (https://lemelson.mit.edu/resources/harry-coover).

explanation: The chemicals stuck to everything they touched, so the researchers threw the idea out. Years later the same chemist realised that the 'flaw' was a superb product.
